chunks: He said: 'I loved the love of wealth (horses) for the sake of the remembrance of my Lord,' until they were hidden by the veil (of the tent).

key_terms.حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ: The love of wealth/good (specifically horses in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'I loved the love of wealth' in Surah Sad?
ai.summary: This narration, often cited in Shia exegesis regarding Prophet Sulaiman (AS) or the Imams, clarifies that the 'love of good' (wealth/horses) was a means to facilitate readiness for jihad and divine remembrance, rather than mere attachment. The 'veiling' (tawarat) signifies the horses remaining in the tent until the time for prayer or battle, illustrating how material assets can be subordinated to spiritual duties. This highlights the Shia principle of using worldly resources for higher spiritual and communal ends.
